segments.text: Most hackathon demos are a screen recording and an apology. This template turns a repository into a narrated, subtitled demo video from a single command. This is what that command produces.

Here is the usual hackathon demo. Someone records their screen at midnight, whispers over it, and uploads whatever happened. If the app stalls, the take is ruined. If they talk too fast, nobody can read the screen. And there is no way to fix one sentence without recording everything again.

vars.name: RECORDED AT MIDNIGHT.
vars.tagline: ONE TAKE, WHISPERED OVER, UPLOADED AS-IS.
vars.sub: A stalled app ruins the take. A rushed sentence hides the screen.
vars.note: Fixing one line means recording everything again.
vars.meta: the problem: no script · no retakes · no proof it works

segments.text: So instead, you write the story once: a hook, a problem, the product working, proof you can point to, and a close. Every segment gets its own narration, generated locally. Terminal scenes are scripted line by line, so the screen shows exactly what the tool printed.

scene.title: democut - one command to a finished demo

segments.text: Live pages record themselves: scrolls, clicks, typed text, a visible cursor. The build measures every clip against the narration, trims the lead-in, and freezes the last frame when a scene runs short. That is why every segment lands on the beat.

The recorder follows a script, not a mouse. It moves to a section, waits for real text to appear, types into the search box, and clicks what a user would click. If a selector misses, the run prints a warning instead of silently filming the wrong thing. What you see is the actual page, at full size, doing the actual work.

And the result checks itself. The build writes a contact sheet, one frame from every part of the video, plus a frame at the middle of every segment. If a scene is blank, frozen, or out of sync with the narration, you see it in the sheet before anyone else does. Nothing ships on a green checkmark alone.

lines.text: [qa]  duration   reported - length follows the product
[qa]  black gaps  none    short clips  none

segments.text: Then ffmpeg muxes the audio, normalizes the loudness, and burns the subtitles. One file, ready to upload, with a subtitle sidecar for platforms that want it. Copy this folder into your project, rewrite the story, point the scenes at your product, and ship a demo that took minutes, not a weekend.
